title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical errors. Every decomposition is a genuine open-cover union, hence a homotopy pushout, so the identifications are correct up to homotopy (and even up to homeomorphism if the D are taken open).
Notational looseness only: 'P' denotes both the one-point space and the origin. Writing D0* = U1∩U2 conflates the open stratum with its global open set; this is harmless here.

ideas.what: Recovering the homotopy type of open unions of strata of a normal-crossings stratified space as homotopy colimits of open strata, tubular neighbourhoods and deleted neighbourhoods (links).
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy-colimit / van Kampen decomposition of a stratified space; homotopy links; exit-path / stratified homotopy hypothesis.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Mayer–Vietoris, van Kampen). In stratified form: Siebenmann, Quinn (homotopically stratified spaces, 1988), MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν}, tame topology and dévissage of stratified spaces in a programmatic way, without this explicit diagram.

ideas.what: Writing C^2 as the colimit of a 3×3 diagram that is the product of two spans (cubical diagram over the product of stratification posets).
ideas.modern_name: Product of homotopy pushouts; cubical homotopy colimits indexed by the face poset of a normal-crossings divisor.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Goodwillie-style cubical diagrams; Deligne's mixed Hodge theory for normal-crossings complements).

missed.claim: Grothendieck is moving toward a programme that encodes a stratified space (ultimately the boundary of the compactified M_{g,ν}) by a diagram of 'elementary' types, namely strata, links and tubular neighbourhoods. The global types are then recovered as amalgamated sums. This anticipates the exit-path / stratified-homotopy viewpoint, but this page only works out the trivial C^2 case.
missed.quote: Comment ensuite reconstituer p.ex. les "globaux" types canoniques ... qui sont des ouverts globaux de X = C^2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest as an early instance of the idea that the homotopy type of a space is determined by local stratified data. Mathematically it is routine and well known today.

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary, correct homotopy-pushout decompositions of C^2 and its open unions of strata along the coordinate axes. They serve only as a worked toy example inside a larger programme; nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: The label written in the middle of each square in (279) reads 'coc.' or 'loc.'. It is most likely 'coc.' (cocartésien), marking the square as a pushout, rather than 'localement'.
The line before (279) reads roughly 'U1, U2 seront donnés par ...' followed by a word like 'recollement'/'sommes amalgamées'; the transcribed '"vrai" général' is uncertain.
In (279) the arrows to U1 and U2 are dotted and enclosed in parentheses, indicating the induced maps to the pushout, not part of the diagram itself.
The top-right of (278) is partly cut off: U1∩U2 = C*×C*.
